<ExternalIntegrationHeader integration={{"name":"Zendure","description":"Connect your Zendure solar batteries (SolarFlow) to Gladys Assistant through the Zendure cloud.","owner":"Terdious","owner_avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/35010958?v=4","repo_url":"https://github.com/Terdious/gladys-zendure","cover_url":"https://integration-store-storage.gladysassistant.com/covers/Terdious--gladys-zendure.png","type":"device","version":"1.13.0","gladys_version":">=5.1.0","stars":0,"pushed_at":"2026-10-23T08:54:28Z"}} />

Connect your **Zendure SolarFlow / Hyper** solar batteries to Gladys Assistant.
Gathers read-only telemetry (battery level, charge/discharge power, home output
and solar production) from the Zendure cloud, and — optionally — directly from
each device's **local MQTT broker** for LAN-speed, offline-resilient updates
with automatic cloud fallback.

Each battery is read and driven through its **local API** (zenSDK) when it
answers on your network — the way Home Assistant does it — with the Zendure
cloud as an automatic fallback.

## Prerequisites

- A **Zendure account**, with your batteries already set up and online in the
  Zendure app.
- Gladys Assistant **5.1 or later**.

## Supported models

SolarFlow 800, SolarFlow 800 Pro, SolarFlow 1600, SolarFlow 2400,
SolarFlow 2400 AC, SolarFlow 2400 Pro, and Hyper 2000 (experimental — telemetry
mapping to be confirmed by a community tester).

**Untested hardware**: SolarFlow 800 Plus, SolarFlow 800 Pro 2 and
SolarFlow 4000 AC+ are supported from the ratings of the official Home
Assistant integration (Zendure-HA), without a real device seen yet. If you own
one, please report how it behaves (a **Diagnostic of the batteries** report is
ideal) on the [issues](https://github.com/Terdious/gladys-zendure/issues).

The model name the Zendure cloud reports is matched ignoring case and spaces
(`SolarFlow 800 Pro`, `SolarFlow800Pro`), like Zendure-HA does.

## Features

Each battery is created with ten read-only features (plus the model-dependent ones below), in the Gladys energy
categories (energy charts, history, dashboards):

| Feature                   | Gladys category          | Unit |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------ | ---- |
| Battery level             | Battery storage          | %    |
| Battery charge power      | Battery storage          | W    |
| Battery discharge power   | Battery storage          | W    |
| Home output power         | Home output sensor       | W    |
| Solar input power         | Energy production sensor | W    |
| Battery charged energy    | Battery storage          | kWh  |
| Battery discharged energy | Battery storage          | kWh  |
| Home output energy        | Home output sensor       | kWh  |
| Solar energy              | Energy production sensor | kWh  |
| Battery energy remaining  | Battery storage          | kWh  |

Zendure reports powers only: the four **energy** features (kWh) are computed
by the integration, which adds up each power over time. They are cumulative
indexes, saved in the integration's data volume so a restart does not reset
them; a silence of more than 5 minutes (battery offline, broker down) is left
out instead of being guessed. Gladys turns the **solar energy** index into
its energy production charts. The **energy remaining** is the state of charge
times the capacity of the packs the battery reports (AB1000, AB2000, AB3000,
built-in packs); it stays empty until the battery sends its pack list.

Since version 1.3.0 the battery level is a **battery storage** level, not the
battery of a device to replace: Gladys no longer counts your home battery in
its low-battery alerts. A battery created with an older version keeps its
previous categories until you apply the new definition: in the **Discover**
tab, click **Update** on the battery (marked **Already added**). The features
are updated in place, so their history, scenes and dashboards are kept. The
same **Update** adds the energy features to a battery created before version
1.5.0.

### Off-grid output, grid charging and temperatures

Depending on the model, a battery also gets these features:

| Feature                  | Gladys category           | Unit | Models                                                              |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------- | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Off-grid output power    | Home output sensor        | W    | 800 Pro, 800 Pro 2, 1600 AC+, 2400 AC, 2400 AC+, 2400 Pro, 4000 AC+ |
| Off-grid output energy   | Home output sensor        | kWh  | same                                                                |
| Grid charging power      | Grid sensor               | W    | every model (AC charging)                                           |
| Grid charging energy     | Grid sensor               | kWh  | every model                                                         |
| Device temperature       | Device temperature sensor | °C   | every model, when reported                                          |
| Hottest pack temperature | Device temperature sensor | °C   | every model, when reported                                          |
| Remaining discharge time | Duration                  | min  | every model with a battery, when estimated                          |
| Remaining charge time    | Duration                  | min  | every model with a battery, when estimated                          |

- **Off-grid output**: the power on the battery's off-grid (backup) socket
  (`gridOffPower`). A negative value means the socket feeds power in (a solar
  panel plugged there, as Zendure-HA notes): it shows 0 and is not counted.
- **Grid charging**: the power the battery draws from the grid to charge
  (`gridInputPower`), on every model able to charge from AC.
- The two **energy** features are computed like the others (power over time,
  saved in the integration's data volume, silences over 5 minutes left out).
- **Temperatures**: the device temperature (`hyperTmp`) and the highest
  temperature of the packs (`maxTemp`), reported by Zendure in tenths of a
  kelvin and converted to °C. A battery that does not report them leaves them
  empty; an impossible value (below −40 °C or above 120 °C) is ignored.
- **Remaining time**: the time to the discharge floor (`remainOutTime`) and
  to the charge target (`remainInputTime`), as the battery estimates it, in
  minutes. When the battery has no estimate (idle, or charging for the
  discharge time), Zendure reports 999 h: that value is not published, the
  feature keeps its last estimate and its last update time shows how old it
  is (0 would read "empty now" and trigger your scenes, 999 h would flatten
  the charts). A SolarFlow 800 or Hyper 2000 without any pack publishes
  nothing.

**Energy hierarchy — avoid double counting.** The grid charging power is a
**grid sensor**: if your home already has a main meter (Linky, a P1 or
Shelly EM meter...) in Gladys, the battery's grid charging is already inside
what that meter measures. In the energy settings of Gladys, place the battery
**under the main meter** (as a child of it), not beside it, or the energy it
draws would be counted twice.

A battery created with an earlier version gets these features with the same
**Update** in the **Discover** tab: the existing features, their history,
scenes and dashboards are kept.

### Battery packs as separate devices (optional)

Off by default. With **Battery packs as separate devices** on (Configuration
tab), the **Discover** tab also lists one device per battery pack, named after
its battery: `Attic battery — pack 1`, `Attic battery — pack 2`… Each pack
device is identified by the pack's own serial number, so its identifiers never
collide with the battery's.

| Feature          | Gladys category           | Unit | Source                                  |
| ---------------- | ------------------------- | ---- | --------------------------------------- |
| Pack level       | Battery                   | %    | `socLevel`                              |
| Pack temperature | Device temperature sensor | °C   | `maxTemp` (hottest cell)                |
| Pack voltage     | Energy sensor             | V    | `totalVol`                              |
| Pack current     | Energy sensor             | A    | `batcur`, signed as the pack reports it |
| Pack power       | Energy sensor             | W    | `power`, when the pack reports it       |

- A pack appears once its battery has listed it: in its reports (local API,
  Zendure cloud, local broker) or in the Zendure device list. If a pack is
  missing, open the **Discover** tab again after a few minutes.
- The values come from the source serving the battery: the pack list of the
  local API or cloud report (raw values, converted: hundredths of a volt,
  tenths of an ampere, tenths of a kelvin), or the pack's own local MQTT
  topics `Zendure/sensor/<pack serial>/…` (values already in V, A, °C). They
  go through the same paced channel as the battery's.
- The battery itself stays the device that counts in the Gladys energy
  features. That is why the pack level is a plain **Battery** level, not a
  home battery level (the battery's own level already is one: counting each
  pack again would count the same charge twice), and why the voltage, current
  and power are plain measurements: keep the pack devices **out of the energy
  hierarchy** of Gladys. The one side effect: if you enabled the Gladys
  low-battery notification, a pack below its threshold at check time is
  mentioned in it.
- The state of health of the packs stays in the diagnostic.
- **Turning the option off creates nothing new and deletes nothing**: the pack
  devices already created stay in Gladys with their history, but no longer
  update. Delete them in Gladys if you no longer want them (see
  [Deleting a battery](#deleting-a-battery)): the integration then ignores them.

## Getting your Zendure cloud key

The integration authenticates against the Zendure cloud with an **authorization
key** (a base64 token) that you generate once from the Zendure mobile app:

1. Open the **Zendure** mobile app and sign in with your account.
2. Go to the developer / Home Assistant integration section of the app and
   generate (or copy) your **authorization key** (also called the "HA key").
3. Copy that key.

> The key is a secret tied to your Zendure account: keep it private. Gladys
> stores it encrypted and never logs it.

## Configuration

1. Open the **Configuration** tab of the integration in Gladys.
2. Paste your key into **Zendure cloud authorization key**.
3. Set the **Refresh interval** (seconds) — how often the telemetry is refreshed
   when no real-time update is flowing. The default (30 s) is fine.
4. (Optional) Enable **local MQTT (zenSDK)** — see below.
5. (Optional) Choose the language of the **Feature names** (English by default):
   it applies to the batteries you create from now on.
6. (Optional) Turn on **Battery packs as separate devices** for one more
   device per pack (off by default) — see
   [Battery packs as separate devices](#battery-packs-as-separate-devices-optional).
7. (Three-phase site) In **Electrical installation**, set **Electrical
   layout** to _Three-phase_ and put each battery in **Phase L1 batteries**,
   **Phase L2 batteries** or **Phase L3 batteries**, the phase it feeds. The
   **Zendure site** and **Energy today** widgets read it from here (see
   [Dashboard widgets](#dashboard-widgets)). A single-phase site leaves it as
   is.
8. Click **Save configuration**. Your batteries appear in the **Discover** tab,
   ready to be added.

### Local API (zenSDK, on by default)

The SolarFlow batteries (800, 800 Plus, 800 Pro, 800 Pro 2, 1600 AC+, 2400 AC,
2400 AC+, 2400 Pro, 4000 AC+
— every supported model but the Hyper 2000) serve a small **HTTP API on your
home network**, called zenSDK. It is what the official Home Assistant integration uses for
these models: neither MQTT nor the cloud. With **Use the local API of the
batteries** on (the default), the integration reads every battery through it
every 5 seconds, and sends the scene and widget commands through it too.

- **Prerequisites**: the battery and the Gladys host on the **same network**
  (the container must be able to reach the battery's IP address: no isolated
  guest Wi-Fi or VLAN in between), and a recent firmware: update the battery
  from the Zendure app if its local API does not answer. Model-specific steps,
  when there are any, are on the
  [Zendure-HA wiki](https://github.com/Zendure/Zendure-HA/wiki) (e.g. its
  [SolarFlow 800 page](https://github.com/Zendure/Zendure-HA/wiki/SolarFlow-800)).
- **Address**: the integration takes the battery's IP address from the Zendure
  cloud. When the cloud gives none, it tries the battery's mDNS name
  `zendure-<model>-<serial number>.local`, which rarely resolves inside a
  Docker container: fill in **Local API addresses** with
  `serial number=IP address` pairs, separated by commas (e.g.
  `HOA1NAH4N123456=192.168.1.42`). Giving your batteries a fixed IP address
  in your router helps.
- **Automatic fallback**: a battery that misses three requests in a row goes
  to its local MQTT broker if you enabled it, at once; it only goes to the
  Zendure cloud after 90 seconds without an answer (a Wi-Fi blip does not
  take the cloud connection), and comes back as soon as its local API answers
  again. At startup, a battery gets the same 90 seconds to give its first
  answer. A battery that never
  answered simply stays on the cloud, without any warning badge.
- **The cloud stays idle**: when every battery answers locally, the
  integration does not connect to the Zendure cloud broker at all, so Home
  Assistant (or another app) using the same Zendure account keeps the account's
  single cloud connection.

### Local MQTT (recommended if you use it)

When you enable local MQTT in the Zendure app (developer mode), each device
publishes its telemetry to a local broker on your network. Turning on **Enable
local MQTT** in Gladys makes the integration read from that broker:

- **Faster**: local values update every 1–3 s instead of ~30 s over the cloud.
- **Resilient**: telemetry keeps flowing during a Zendure cloud or internet
  outage.
- **Automatic fallback**: if a device goes silent on the local broker, the
  integration falls back to the cloud on its own, and returns to local as soon
  as local messages resume — no action needed.

## Transport badges

Each device shows a badge telling you **how it is currently reached**:

- **Local** (green) — served by its local MQTT broker (nominal when local MQTT
  is enabled).
- **Cloud** (blue) — served by the Zendure cloud (nominal when local MQTT is
  off).
- **Cloud + orange dot (degraded)** — the device _should_ be local but is
  temporarily on the cloud fallback (its local broker went silent). Hover the
  badge for the reason. This clears by itself when the device resumes locally.
- **Unreachable** (red) — the Zendure cloud reports the device offline, or it is
  silent on every source.

With the local API, **Local** means its local API or its local broker
serves the device. The degraded reason tells which local source went silent.

## Control from scenes

Gladys has no battery setpoint feature yet, so the batteries are controlled
from **scenes** (and from the dashboard widget): in a scene, add an action of
the **Integrations** category.

| Action                    | What it does                                                 |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Set the output limit**  | Maximum power the battery delivers to the home (W)           |
| **Set the charge limit**  | Maximum power the battery draws from the grid, AC charge (W) |
| **Set the AC mode**       | Charge from the grid, or discharge to the home               |
| **Set the charge levels** | Charge target (70-100 %) and discharge floor (0-50 %)        |

The integration protects the battery:

- a limit is clamped to the battery's rating (e.g. 800 W out on a SolarFlow
  800 Pro);
- power limits are sent in "smart mode", kept in memory instead of being
  written to the battery's flash (frequent changes would wear it out);
- one setting cannot change more than once every 3 s (power limits) or 30 s
  (AC mode, charge levels): a scene that tries sooner fails with the delay to
  wait;
- a value the battery already runs with is not sent again (the action output
  **Command sent** is then false);
- the charge levels are refused until the battery has reported its current
  ones (its scale differs between firmwares).

The command goes through the broker that currently serves the battery (local
or cloud); the new value shows up with the battery's next report.

The trigger **Battery reachability changed** starts a scene when a battery
stops reporting on every source, or reports again (local API or local MQTT). Its
variables give the battery name, the new state and the telemetry source.

The trigger **Battery alert** starts a scene when a status code of a battery
starts or ends. Its filters, all optional (left empty: any value):

- **Battery**: one battery;
- **Alert**: _Fault_ (error flag `is_error`, or fault level `faultLevel` above
  0), _Heating_ (the pack heater runs, `heatState`), _Calibration_ (the
  state-of-charge calibration runs, `socStatus`), _Low temperature_
  (`lowTemperature`), _Reverse flow_ (`reverseState`);
- **Change**: _Started_ or _Ended_.

Its variables give the battery name, the alert, the change (`started` /
`ended`), the code reported (the fault level for a fault) and the telemetry
source (`local` / `cloud`). Examples:

- notify when a battery heats: trigger **Battery alert**, Alert _Heating_,
  Change _Started_, then a **Send a message** action naming the battery from
  the variables;
- notify of a fault, and when it clears: one scene with Alert _Fault_ and
  Change _Started_, another with Change _Ended_.

An alert fires on a change only: the state a battery is in when the
integration starts (or when it is created again) is its initial state, not an
event. A new state must hold for 30 seconds, over at least two reports, before
the scene starts: a code that blinks for a report never does. A battery
deleted in Gladys and the pack devices fire no alert.

## Dashboard widgets

Four widgets are available in the dashboard editor (Gladys 5.1 or later):

- **Zendure battery**: one battery, chosen in the widget settings. Its four
  powers follow the battery live; its charge level and the lines below
  refresh every two minutes (it moves by about 1 % a minute at most): its source
  (local, cloud, fallback, unreachable), the energy stored, the output and
  charge limits, the AC mode and the charge levels it reports. The **Power
  limits** and **Mode & levels** buttons open a form pre-filled with the
  current values: change what you need and confirm. The same protections as
  the scene actions apply.
- **Battery group**: several batteries summed up under a name of your choice:
  average charge level (weighted by the pack capacities when they are all
  known), total powers, energy stored, a live chart, and one line per battery
  colored by its source, listed by name (see **Charts and list order** below).
  Leave the battery list empty for every battery of the account.
- **Zendure site**: the whole installation on one card. Choose the
  **Electrical layout**: _From the integration configuration_ (the default,
  recommended) uses the layout and the phases of the **Electrical
  installation** section of the configuration; _Single-phase_ sums the
  batteries selected in the widget (none: all of them); _Three-phase_ takes
  the batteries of the widget's **Phase L1 batteries**, **L2** and **L3**
  lists. The card shows the site totals (state of charge
  weighted by the pack capacities, charging, discharging, solar, home output,
  energy stored), then in three-phase one line per phase (`⌂` home output,
  `↑` charge, `↓` discharge, `☀` solar, in W) and the **Phase balance**: the
  gap between the highest and the lowest home output, in orange beyond the
  **Phase imbalance alert** (500 W by default). Below: stored energy over the
  known capacity, time left at the current power, how many batteries each
  source serves (local, cloud, unreachable), and alert lines for the
  unreachable batteries, the cloud fallbacks, and a battery put in two phases,
  in none, or deleted. An unreachable battery keeps its level and stored
  energy, but its last powers are left out of the sums.
- **Energy today**: the energy of the day since local midnight, same layout
  choice and phase lists: charged, discharged, solar and home output (kWh),
  one line per phase in three-phase with the gap between the phases, and a
  chart per 30 minutes of the flow chosen in **Chart** (home output by
  default, one curve per phase). The day
  starts at the midnight of the widget's **Timezone** (an IANA name,
  `Europe/Paris` by default: Gladys does not give its timezone to an
  integration). The figures come from the energy counters of the integration
  (saved under `/data` with a snapshot every 30 minutes, kept 8 days): they
  count from the first report of the day, which the **Counted since** line
  shows (for example after a first install in the morning).
  With an electricity tariff in the configuration, it also shows the savings
  estimate (see **Savings (estimate)** below).

**Three-phase example:** 18 batteries on L1, L2 and L3. In the **Configuration**
tab, section **Electrical installation**, set **Electrical layout** to
_Three-phase_ and tick in **Phase L1 batteries** the six batteries wired to L1
(say two 2400 AC, a 2400 Pro, two 800 Pro and an 800 without battery), in
**Phase L2 batteries** the six of L2 and in **Phase L3 batteries** the six of
L3, then save. Add a **Zendure site** widget and an **Energy today** widget,
and keep their **Electrical layout** on _From the integration configuration_:
there is nothing else to pick. The site card shows the site totals, a line
such as `L1 (6) · 60 %` — `⌂ 1890 · ↑ 500 · ↓ 1000 · ☀ 1400 W` per phase, and
`Phase balance` — `Δ 1490 W · L1 highest` in orange when it exceeds the
threshold; the energy card the kWh of the day per phase. A single-phase
installation keeps the defaults everywhere. The **Battery group** widget still
works for any other grouping.

**Why the phases live in the configuration:** Gladys keeps at most 1 KB of
settings per widget, and each battery picked in a widget list takes about 50
characters (its identifier). Past about 15 batteries in the widget lists, the
widget can no longer be displayed nor the dashboard saved (error 422
_settings: must be at most 1024 bytes_). The configuration has no such limit,
and the phases are set once for both widgets. A widget set to _From the
integration configuration_ while the configuration is three-phase without any
battery assigned shows every battery as single-phase, with a **No phase
assigned** warning line; phases filled in a single-phase configuration are
ignored (**Phases ignored** line). Widgets set to _Single-phase_ or
_Three-phase_ before keep their own lists and keep working. A widget already over the limit: remove it from the dashboard and add it again (or empty its lists), keeping _From the integration configuration_.

**Charts and list order:** the **Battery group** and **Zendure site** widgets
draw a live chart of the last hours, chosen in their **Chart** setting:
_Powers_ (charge, discharge, solar and home output summed up), _Power to the
home_, _Charge level_ (weighted by the pack capacities) or _No chart_, over
the **Chart period** (3, 6, 12 or 24 hours, 6 by default). On a three-phase
site, _Power to the home_ (the default of the site widget) and _Charge level_
draw one curve per phase (L1, L2, L3). The integration records these values
itself every 5 minutes for the last 48 hours (under `/data`, with the energy
counters): after an update, the curves fill in from that moment. Gladys keeps
8 elements per widget, buttons included: the tiles that do not fit become the
first lines of the card (the stored energy of the site card stays in its
**Stored / capacity** line). A widget shows its name as a heading only when
its **Title** is filled in: the card already names it. The **Energy today** chart offers _To the home_,
_Charged_, _Discharged_, _Solar_ (one curve per phase in three-phase), _All
the flows of the site_ or _No chart_. The battery lines of a group follow its
**Order of the list**: _By name_ (the default, in natural order: `L1.2` before
`L1.10`, the same on every phase), _As selected_, highest _Charge level_ or
highest _Power to the home_ first.

**Periods and navigation:** every widget with a chart carries a **Period**
button and **Previous** / **Next** buttons, like the charts of Gladys. On the
**Battery group** and **Zendure site** widgets, the period is 3, 6, 12 or 24
hours (the **Chart period** setting is the one shown first), and **Previous**
steps back by one period, as far as the last 48 hours. On **Energy today**,
the period is a day or 7 days (one bar per day): **Previous** goes back day
by day, or week by week, over the last 8 days, and a past period shows a
**Shown** line with its dates. The tiles and lines follow the period shown
(the energy of that day or week, per phase); the savings estimate shows on
today only. The period is kept per widget until the integration restarts,
then the widget goes back to its default period. The **Period** button opens
a form on Gladys 5.2 or later; on an older core, each tap moves to the next
period. Zendure keeps no longer history: no month nor year view.

**Placing them:** the site and energy widgets are made to show the whole
installation: put them in a dashboard section with one or two columns, where
the chart and the per-phase lines get the width they need. The battery and
group widgets fit a three-column section (one group per phase, for example).

Each widget only shows what the battery has: a SolarFlow 800 running
without a battery pack keeps its solar, home output and output limit (no
level, charge figures nor **Mode & levels** button), and an AC-coupled model
(1600 AC+, 2400 AC, 2400 AC+) has no solar tile. While a battery charges or
discharges, the widget shows the time left until its charge target or its
discharge floor, as the battery reports it (or computed from its capacity when
it gives none). A group leaves the batteries without a pack out of its average
level and stored energy, and a group of such devices only shows their powers.

## Savings (estimate)

With your electricity tariff, the integration **estimates** what your
batteries save, every 30 minutes, per battery, and the **Energy today**
widget sums it for its batteries (the site, or each phase). It is an
**estimate without a grid meter**, marked as such in the widget: read the
limits below.

### Setting the tariff

In the **Configuration** tab, section **Savings (estimate, no grid meter)**:

- **Electricity tariff**: _None_ (the default: no estimate), _Base_ (one
  price) or _Peak / off-peak_.
- **Base price**, or **Peak price** and **Off-peak price**: the price of one
  kWh bought from the grid, taxes included (for example `0.1952`). A missing
  price turns the estimate off.
- **Off-peak hours**: `HH:MM-HH:MM` ranges separated by commas, for example
  `22:00-06:00` or `01:30-07:30,12:30-14:30`. A range may cross midnight;
  `24:00` is accepted as an end. Invalid hours turn the estimate off: the
  logs and the diagnostic say why (once), and the widget shows _Tariff
  invalid_.
- **I sell my solar surplus** and **Resale price**: on, the solar energy
  stored in the batteries is valued at the resale price (what it would have
  earned on the grid); off, stored solar energy is free.
- **Tariff timezone** (IANA name, `Europe/Paris` by default): the off-peak
  hours, and the days, months and years of the savings, follow it, clock
  changes included. It is a setting of the integration and not of the widget
  because the slots are valued in the background, as they close, when no
  widget is open; the widget's own **Timezone** still sets the midnight of
  its energy figures.

In the **Energy today** widget, **Show the savings (estimate)** is on by
default: it only shows something once a tariff is set.

### How it is computed

For each battery and each 30-minute slot, from its energy counters:

- **Price of the slot**: the base price, or the peak / off-peak price at the
  local time of the slot (a slot straddling the edge of a range is priced pro
  rata).
- **Cost of the stored energy**: a weighted average per battery. The energy
  charged from the grid (the **Grid charging energy** counter) costs the
  price of the slot; the rest of the charge, from the solar panels, costs the
  resale price when you sell your surplus, 0 otherwise. The stored energy is
  re-read from the state of charge when the packs are known.
- **Home output**: without a grid meter the integration cannot know what was
  exported, so the energy sent to the home is **assumed consumed** by the
  house. Its share coming from the battery saves _price of the slot − cost of
  the stored energy_ (a battery charged at peak and discharged off-peak saves
  less than nothing); its share coming straight from the solar panels saves
  the price of the slot; the rest (grid passing through an AC battery) saves
  nothing.
- **Savings** = battery time-shift + direct solar (+ resale revenue, with the
  grid meter). The **Grid charging (paid)** line is information: that cost is
  already inside the cost of the stored energy.

The widget shows **Saved today (estimate)**, the month and the year, today
per phase in three-phase, and today's breakdown (battery time-shift, direct
solar, grid charging paid, export). The totals of the current and previous
day, month and year are saved in `/data/energy.json` with the energy
counters (a file from an earlier version loads as is; the savings start at
the first 30-minute boundary after the update).

### Limits

- **No knowledge of the export**: the home output sent back to the grid
  (house consumption below the battery output) is counted as saved at the
  price of the slot. The **Exported, not valued** line (or **Resale** when
  you sell) stays at 0 until the grid meter can be read.
- **AC batteries** (1600 AC+, 2400 AC, 2400 AC+, 4000 AC+): their AC charging
  is counted as **grid charging** at the price of the slot, even when it
  actually comes from the solar surplus of another inverter: only the site
  balance (the grid meter) could tell.
- Pack losses, conversion losses and missed reports make the figures
  approximate; the savings start when the tariff is set (nothing is computed
  backwards), and a tariff change applies to the slots that close afterwards.
- The currency is the one of your prices; the widget writes `€`.

### Coming soon

Two options will appear in the configuration once Gladys offers them to
integrations (Gladys changes in progress:
[#3229](https://github.com/GladysAssistant/Gladys/pull/3229) and
[#3230](https://github.com/GladysAssistant/Gladys/pull/3230)):

- **Use the prices of Gladys energy monitoring**, instead of typing them here.
- **Grid meter** (single-phase, or three-phase L1 / L2 / L3): to know what is
  really consumed or exported, value the resale and the losses, and tell the
  solar surplus from grid charging on the AC batteries.

## One cloud consumer per Zendure account

Zendure allows **only one cloud consumer per account** at a time. If another app
uses the same account's cloud connection (Home Assistant, a second Gladys
instance…), the two fight over the connection and telemetry becomes
intermittent. Prefer the **local MQTT** path for any second consumer — the local
broker has no such limit. The integration warns once in its logs when it detects
this take-over pattern.

With the **local API** on (the default), the integration only connects to the
Zendure cloud broker while a battery needs it, and disconnects again 5 minutes
after the last battery that needed it is back on a local source: if your batteries answer
locally, Home Assistant and Gladys no longer fight over the cloud connection.

## Deleting a battery

Deleting a battery in Gladys (its device page, **Delete**) stops everything the
integration does for it, at once and without a restart: its local API is no
longer polled, its broker topics are unsubscribed, it no longer counts for the
cloud fallback (the cloud broker is released right away when no other battery
needs it, so Home Assistant gets the account's cloud session back), and it
leaves the watchdog logs, the dashboard widgets, the scene actions and the
diagnostic (which lists it once as ignored). The logs say it in one line:
`1 device(s) ignored (deleted in Gladys): …`.

The list of deleted batteries is saved with the integration configuration in
Gladys, so a restart or an update does not bring them back. The battery stays in
the **Discover** tab: create it again there and it is tracked again at once, under
the same identifiers.

## Updating the integration

**Installed from the catalog** (the usual case): Gladys checks the store
regularly. When a new version is out, the integration shows an **"Update
available"** badge (also counted next to **Integrations** in the menu), and its
**Supervision** tab names the version offered, with a link to its release
notes. Click **Update**: Gladys pulls the new image **and** applies the new
manifest — new configuration fields appear on their own, there is nothing to
re-paste. Your configuration and your devices are kept.

Gladys can take up to about an hour and a half to notice a new release (store
index refresh). **"Force update"** checks right away: it reads the latest
published version and pulls its image.

**Installed in developer mode** (manifest pasted by hand): **"Force update"**
only re-pulls the image of the tag you installed, and the version shown and the
configuration fields come from the pasted manifest — re-paste the updated
manifest to pick up new fields.

## Troubleshooting

- **A battery is not discovered.** Open the **Logs** tab: a line `Unsupported
Zendure model skipped: productModel "..."` gives the exact model string the
  Zendure cloud reports. Open an issue on
  [gladys-zendure](https://github.com/Terdious/gladys-zendure/issues) with it,
  so the model can be added.
- **One device shows no values (or is slower than the others) while the rest
  work.** Check its transport badge. If it fell back to **Cloud (degraded)**
  while local MQTT is enabled, its firmware may have silently stopped publishing
  locally. In the Zendure app, toggle that device's **MQTT control OFF**, save,
  then **ON** again — it resumes publishing within a minute. The integration
  falls back to the cloud in the meantime and returns to local automatically.
- **`Too Many Requests` in the logs.** The integration paces its updates under
  the Gladys core rate limit and self-throttles when needed; occasional bursts
  are harmless. Persistent floods usually mean a **second integration instance**
  (e.g. a prod and a test container side by side) sharing the same core budget —
  run only one.
- **Everything is silent right after configuration.** Make sure the cloud key is
  correct: an invalid or expired key shows a "Zendure cloud is unreachable or
  the cloud key is invalid" status on the Configuration screen.
- **Full detail.** Set `LOG_LEVEL=debug` and read the integration logs in its
  **Logs** tab (or `docker logs` on the host). Every telemetry-source switch is
  logged on a `telemetry:` line.
- **A battery stays on the cloud although its local API should work.** At
  startup the logs list every battery that does not answer, with the address
  tried and the reason, e.g. `local http: Garage (dCLTD95V) not answering at
192.168.1.42 (from the cloud): EHOSTUNREACH`. `ENOTFOUND` on a `.local`
  name means mDNS does not resolve in the container: set its address in
  **Local API addresses**. `EHOSTUNREACH`, `ECONNREFUSED` or `no answer
within 2 s` mean the container cannot reach the battery (other network,
  VLAN, firewall) or its firmware has no local API yet. Every 5 minutes a
  `telemetry(local http):` line sums up which batteries answer.

### Diagnostic

Two read-only buttons in the **Configuration** tab of the integration rebuild
the whole picture on demand, so you do not have to dig through the logs.
Neither writes to a battery nor changes its transport.

- **Diagnostic of the batteries**: a text report of the installation — the
  integration version, the configuration (never the cloud key), the Zendure
  cloud API, each broker (connected or not, reconnections over the last
  5 minutes, cloud broker idle because every battery is local, take-over
  warnings), the local API polling, then one block per battery: the source
  serving it and why, the age of its last data on each source, its local API
  address (from the options, the cloud or mDNS) and state, battery packs,
  solar input, the settings it reports (limits, AC mode, charge levels),
  remaining time and energy counters, then the firmware versions (device,
  master, DSP, packs), the Wi-Fi signal (`rssi`, with a hint below −75 dBm)
  and connection states, the raw status codes (heating, low temperature, SoC
  calibration and limit, bypass, HEMS, fault level) and per pack its level,
  hottest cell temperature, voltage, current and state of health. Pick a battery in the **Battery** list
  (the batteries created in Gladys) to report on it only; for a battery not
  created in Gladys, type its name or serial number in the field below.
- **Test the local API of a battery**: reads `GET /properties/report` once,
  right away, at the address the integration uses, and shows the answer time,
  where the address comes from and every property the battery returns — or the
  exact error with a hint (`ENOTFOUND` on a `.local` name: fill **Local API
  addresses**; `EHOSTUNREACH`, `ECONNREFUSED` or a timeout: network or
  firmware).

By default serial numbers are shortened (`WOB1…0159`) and local addresses
replaced by `<local-ip>`: paste the report as is into a
[GitHub issue](https://github.com/Terdious/gladys-zendure/issues), between two
lines of three backticks. **Show serial numbers and local addresses** prints
them in full, for your own checks only: do not post that version publicly.
No report ever contains the cloud key or a password. Both reports are also
written, masked, to the integration logs.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Zendure asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Getting started | `section` | No | Paste your Zendure cloud authorization key below (generated from the Zendure mobile app). Your SolarFlow / Hyper batteries then appear in the Discover tab. Each battery is then served by its local API when it answers on your network (like Home Assistant does), with automatic Zendure cloud fallback; local MQTT remains an option for older firmwares. The full step-by-step is in the Documentation link above. |
| Zendure cloud authorization key | `secret` | Yes | The authorization key generated from the Zendure mobile app (base64 token used to reach the Zendure cloud API). |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | No | How often device telemetry is polled, in seconds. |
| Use the local API of the batteries | `boolean` | No | Read and drive each battery through its zenSDK local HTTP API on your network (what Home Assistant uses), every few seconds. A battery that does not answer stays on the Zendure cloud, automatically. |
| Local API addresses (optional) | `string` | No | Only for a battery whose local API is not found (no address from the cloud, mDNS name not resolved): serial number=IP address pairs, separated by commas. |
| Enable local MQTT (zenSDK) | `boolean` | No | Also read telemetry from the device's local MQTT broker when available (older firmwares, Hyper 2000), before the Zendure cloud. |
| Feature names | `select` | No | Language of the feature names given to newly discovered batteries. A battery already created keeps its names: rename its features in Gladys if needed. |
| Battery packs as separate devices | `boolean` | No | Off by default. On: the Discover tab also lists one device per battery pack (level, temperature, voltage, current, power), named after its battery. Turning it off creates nothing new and deletes nothing: pack devices already created stay, and stop updating. |
| Electrical installation | `section` | No | Used by the "Zendure site" and "Energy today" dashboard widgets set to "From the integration configuration" (their default). On a three-phase site, put each battery in the phase it feeds (L1, L2, L3): once here, for every widget. The settings of a widget are limited to 1 KB by Gladys, about 15 batteries, so a large site cannot keep its phases there. |
| Electrical layout | `select` | No | Single-phase: the site widgets total every battery. Three-phase: per phase, from the three lists below. |
| Phase L1 batteries | `multi_select` | No | Three-phase only: each battery in the phase it feeds. |
| Phase L2 batteries | `multi_select` | No | Three-phase only: each battery in the phase it feeds. |
| Phase L3 batteries | `multi_select` | No | Three-phase only: each battery in the phase it feeds. |
| Savings (estimate, no grid meter) | `section` | No | Optional. With your electricity tariff, the integration estimates every 30 minutes what your batteries save: the energy sent to the home is assumed consumed by the house (without a grid meter nothing tells what is exported), valued at the price of the moment, minus the cost of the stored energy (grid charging at its price, solar charging at the resale price or free). The "Energy today" widget shows it for today, this month and this year. Details and limits in the Documentation link above. |
| Electricity tariff | `select` | No | None: no savings estimate. Base: one price. Peak / off-peak: two prices and the off-peak hours. |
| Base price (per kWh) | `number` | No | Base tariff: the price of one kWh bought from the grid, taxes included (€/kWh). |
| Peak price (per kWh) | `number` | No | Peak / off-peak tariff: the price of one kWh outside the off-peak hours, taxes included (€/kWh). |
| Off-peak price (per kWh) | `number` | No | Peak / off-peak tariff: the price of one kWh during the off-peak hours, taxes included (€/kWh). |
| Off-peak hours | `string` | No | HH:MM-HH:MM ranges separated by commas, in the tariff timezone; a range may cross midnight. Invalid hours: the estimate is off (see the logs). |
| I sell my solar surplus | `boolean` | No | On: the solar energy stored in the batteries is valued at the resale price (what it would have earned), and exported energy counts as revenue once a grid meter can be read. Off: stored solar energy is free. |
| Resale price (per kWh) | `number` | No | The price paid for one kWh of solar surplus sent to the grid (€/kWh). Used only when the option above is on. |
| Tariff timezone | `string` | No | IANA name, e.g. Europe/Paris (the default): the off-peak hours and the days, months and years of the savings follow it, clock changes included. |
| Coming soon | `section` | No | Two options will appear here once Gladys offers them to integrations (pending Gladys changes, linked below): "Use the prices of Gladys energy monitoring", instead of the prices above; and "Grid meter (single-phase, or three-phase L1 / L2 / L3)", to know what is really consumed or exported, value the resale and the losses, and tell PV surplus from grid charging on AC batteries. Until then the savings are an estimate. |

## How to install Zendure in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Zendure appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/terdious/gladys-zendure:1.13.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/Terdious/gladys-zendure](https://github.com/Terdious/gladys-zendure).

Zendure requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Zendure is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [Terdious](https://github.com/Terdious), not by the Gladys core team.

- [Browse all integrations](/docs/integrations/), native and community
- [Build and publish your own external integration](/docs/dev/external-integrations/)
- [Source code on GitHub](https://github.com/Terdious/gladys-zendure) — [source of this documentation](https://github.com/Terdious/gladys-zendure/blob/HEAD/docs/en.md)
